plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $36. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a lower bid but higher than my value bid from others; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit since payment is determined by others' bids, not my own.

The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. My value is $33, so I will bid $33 to maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding above my value only risks paying more than the item is worth if I end up setting the price myself relative to others. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. With no prior round history to adjust from, I'll bid my true value of $31.
